questions.title: Flight Ticket
questions.prompt:
Create a class named `FlightTicket` in `FlightTicket.java`:

* **Private fields:** `String passengerName`, `String flightNumber`, `int seatRow`, `double baseFare`.
* **Constructor 1:** `FlightTicket(String passengerName, String flightNumber, int seatRow, double baseFare)`
* **Constructor 2:** `FlightTicket(String passengerName, String flightNumber)` which sets `seatRow` to `30` and `baseFare` to `199.99`.
* **Getters and Setters:** For all four fields.
  * In `setSeatRow(int seatRow)`: A commercial aircraft only has rows 1 to 40 inclusive. If `seatRow < 1`, set `seatRow = 1`. If `seatRow > 40`, set `seatRow = 40`.
  * In `setBaseFare(double baseFare)`: Fare cannot be negative. If `baseFare < 0.0`, set `baseFare = 0.0`.

tests.name: Test 1 [Visible] (Sample Run)
tests.description: 2-arg constructor default fields; upper row clamp (55 -> 40); negative fare clamp (-50.0 -> 0.0).

tests.name: Test 2 [Hidden] (Lower Row Clamp)
tests.description: setSeatRow(0) and setSeatRow(-5) clamp to 1.

tests.name: Test 3 [Hidden] (Row Boundaries)
tests.description: Setting row to exactly 1 and 40 keeps 1 and 40.

tests.name: Test 4 [Hidden] (4-Arg Constructor)
tests.description: new FlightTicket("Neil Armstrong", "UA202", 12, 349.50) preserves all fields.

tests.name: Test 5 [Hidden] (Zero Fare)
tests.description: setBaseFare(0.0) sets baseFare to 0.0.

tests.name: Test 6 [Hidden] (String Setters)
tests.description: setPassengerName and setFlightNumber update fields correctly.

graderCases.name: Sample run (2-arg defaults + clamps)
Lower row clamp
Row boundaries 1 and 40
4-arg constructor preserves fields
Zero fare allowed

t.setBaseFare(0.0); eqD(t.getBaseFare(),0.0);

questions.title: Smart Thermostat
questions.prompt:
Create a class named `Thermostat` in `Thermostat.java`:

* **Private fields:** `String deviceId`, `String roomName`, `double currentTemp`.
* **Constructor:** `Thermostat(String deviceId, String roomName, double currentTemp)`.
* **`toString()`:** Return:
  ```
  Device: <deviceId>
  Room: <roomName>

  ```
  *(Separated by `\n` with no trailing newline)*
* **`equals(Object o)`:** Two thermostats are equal if their `deviceId` matches **ignoring case**, regardless of room name or temperature. Return `false` if `o` is `null` or not an instance of `Thermostat`.

questions.title: Bank Transaction Validator
questions.prompt:
Create a checked exception named `InsufficientFundsException` in `InsufficientFundsException.java` that extends `Exception` with a constructor taking `String message`.

In `AccountValidator.java`, implement:
`public static double processWithdrawal(double balance, double amount) throws InsufficientFundsException`
* If `amount <= 0.0`, throw `IllegalArgumentException` with message: `"Withdrawal amount must be positive"`.
* If `amount > balance`, throw `InsufficientFundsException` with message: `"Overdraft prevented: balance is <balance>, withdrawal requested is <amount>"`. (Use raw double in message).
* Otherwise, return `balance - amount`.

Overdraft prevented: balance is 60.0, withdrawal requested is 75.0

questions.title: Warehouse Payload Manager
questions.prompt:
Given a base class `Container` with method `double getWeight()` and subclass `HeavyContainer` (which has additional tare reinforcement weight included in `getWeight()`), implement `PayloadManager.java`:
* `public static double totalWeight(Container[] containers)`:

  * If `containers` is `null` or empty, return `0.0`.

questions.title: Server Access Log Parser
questions.prompt:
In `LogAnalyzer.java`, write:
`public static int countErrors(String filename, int targetHttpCode) throws FileNotFoundException`

questions.title: Athletic Qualifier Ranking
questions.prompt:
This question gives you a question-specific abstract class **and** a question-specific interface. Your class must extend one and implement the other.

Create an abstract class `Athlete` in `Athlete.java`:
* **Protected fields:** `String name`, `String team`.
* **Constructor:** `Athlete(String name, String team)`.
* **Getters:** `getName()`, `getTeam()`.
* **Abstract method:** `public abstract double rawMetric();` (the athlete's raw timed result).

Create an interface `Rankable` in `Rankable.java`:
* Abstract method: `double rankingScore();` *(higher is always better)*.
* Default method: `default boolean outranks(Rankable other)`: returns `true` only if `this.rankingScore()` is **strictly greater** than `other.rankingScore()`.
* Default method: `default boolean isPodium(double threshold)`: returns `true` if `rankingScore() >= threshold`.

Create a class `SprintAthlete` in `SprintAthlete.java` that **extends `Athlete` and implements `Rankable`**:
* **Private fields:** `double seconds`, `double windMps`.
* **Constructor:** `SprintAthlete(String name, String team, double seconds, double windMps)` calling `super`.
* `rawMetric()` returns `seconds`.
* `rankingScore()`:
  * Base score is `10.0 - seconds`.
  * A tailwind is **legal up to and including 2.0 m/s**. If `windMps > 2.0`, the result is not record-eligible: subtract a `0.5` penalty from the score.
  * Scores may be negative.

*Edge cases to think about (not in the sample): wind of exactly 2.0 is legal; two equal scores must not outrank each other; the podium threshold is inclusive; an illegal tailwind can let a slower-but-legal athlete outrank a faster one.*
questions.expectedOutput:
Raw: 9.91
Score: 0.09
A outranks B: true

questions.title: Musical Instrument Hierarchy
questions.prompt:
This question requires both a question-specific abstract class and a question-specific interface. Your subclasses must extend the class **and** implement the interface.

Create an abstract class `Instrument` in `Instrument.java`:
* **Protected fields:** `String name`, `int baseDecibels`.
* **Constructor:** `Instrument(String name, int baseDecibels)`.
* **Abstract method:** `public abstract int playNote(int intensity);`

Create an interface `Tunable` in `Tunable.java`:
* Abstract method: `int getTranspose();` *(a semitone offset; may be negative)*.
* Default method: `default boolean isConcertPitch()`: returns `true` only when `getTranspose() == 0`.
* Default method: `default int pitchClass()`: folds the transpose into one octave, **always returning a value in `[0, 11]` even for negative transposes** (e.g. `-1` → `11`).

Create `Brass` in `Brass.java` **extending `Instrument` and implementing `Tunable`**:
* **Private field:** `int transpose`.
* **Constructor:** `Brass(String name, int baseDecibels, int transpose)` calling `super`.
* `playNote(int intensity)`: `baseDecibels + (intensity * 4)`; if `intensity > 10`, add a `15` dB brass distortion penalty.
* `getTranspose()` returns `transpose`.

Create `Woodwind` in `Woodwind.java` **extending `Instrument` and implementing `Tunable`**:
* **Private field:** `int transpose`.
* **Constructor:** `Woodwind(String name, int baseDecibels, int transpose)` calling `super`.
* `playNote(int intensity)`: `baseDecibels + (intensity * 2)`, capped at `95` dB.
* `getTranspose()` returns `transpose`.

*Edge cases to think about (not in the sample): intensity exactly 10 (no brass penalty); a woodwind landing exactly on 95; `pitchClass()` for negative transposes must wrap into `[0,11]`.*

questions.title: Submarine Dive Controller
questions.prompt:
This capstone requires a question-specific abstract class **and** a question-specific interface, extended/implemented together by your concrete class.

Create an abstract class `Submersible` in `Submersible.java`:
* **Protected fields:** `String callSign`, `int depth`, `int integrity`.
* **Constructor:** `Submersible(String callSign)` starts at `depth = 0`, `integrity = 100`.
* **Getters:** `getDepth()`, `getIntegrity()`.
* Method `isLost()`: returns `true` when `integrity <= 0`.
* **Abstract method:** `public abstract void dive(int meters);`
* Concrete method `surface(int meters)`: subtract `meters` from `depth`, clamped so `depth` never drops below `0`.

Create an interface `DepthLimited` in `DepthLimited.java`:
* Abstract method: `int crushDepth();`
* Default method: `default boolean isImplodeRisk(int currentDepth)`: `true` only when `currentDepth` is **strictly greater** than `crushDepth()`.
* Default method: `default int safetyMargin(int currentDepth)`: `crushDepth() - currentDepth`, but **never negative** (floored at `0`).

Create a class `AttackSub` in `AttackSub.java` **extending `Submersible` and implementing `DepthLimited`**:
* **Private field:** `int crush` (the crush depth, provided in the constructor).
* **Constructor:** `AttackSub(String callSign, int crushDepth)` calling `super(callSign)`.
* `crushDepth()` returns `crush`.
* `dive(int meters)`: add `meters` to `depth`. If the **new** depth is strictly greater than `crush`, the hull takes `15` points of damage; `integrity` is floored at `0`.
* Method `emergencyBlow()`: set `depth` back to `0` and deduct `25` integrity (floored at `0`).

*Edge cases to think about (not in the sample): diving to exactly the crush depth does no damage; surfacing past the surface clamps at 0; integrity floors at 0 (never negative) and then `isLost()` is true; `isImplodeRisk` is strict at the boundary; `safetyMargin` never goes negative.*

Depth: 250m | Integrity: 85%
Depth: 0m | Integrity: 60%
